claims.value: For May 3 Colletta gives side A 12,000 and side B at least 16,000, after leaving Lecchi in Macerata; these differ materially from Bodart’s 29,000/11,000.
claims.rationale: Own-side narrative and estimate of opponent, no original local return. Not reconciled with Bodart or the wider pre-battle army distribution. English rendering (ours): "Dawn on the third was obscured by dense fog. New German troops came during the night; Stròngoli arrived, while Lecchi remained at Macerata. The enemy had at least sixteen thousand, on the hills with its right on the Chienti; our line had twelve thousand."

citations.locator: colletta-1856-v2, printed 200, Internet Archive leaf 205; retained full page image inspected
citations.quote: Fu lunga l’alba del 3, coperta da nebbia densissima, che nascondeva i due eserciti. Nella notte nuove schiere tedesche vennero a Tolentino; e per la opposta parte la legion Stròngoli giunse al campo, quella di Lecchi restò in Macerata, per la speranza di volgerla contro Neipperg, bastando tre legioni, nella mente del re, a vincer Bianchi. Ma, diradata la caligine, fu visto fortissimo il nemico (sedicimila uomini almeno) schierato sopra i colli che fan cortina alla città, poggiando il fianco destro al Chienti, il sinistro ad un monte aspro e difficile, ed avendo innanzi al centro due poggi, quasi sporgenti nelle nostre linee. Le quali, obliquamente ordinate dirimpetto al nemico, appoggiavano anch’esse la sinistra al fiume, la diritta al monte; dodicimila soldati.

claims.value: Before the battle Colletta describes the wider Neapolitan army between Cesano and Chienti as 24,000, and Murat’s intended four-legion attack as 16,000. Neither is substituted for the May 3 local line.
claims.rationale: Earlier wider distribution and intended allocation; different times/populations, not additional independent estimates of the same local force. English rendering (ours): "The first legion held Neipperg; four were at Macerata, with small garrisons at Ancona; the whole host was twenty-four thousand. The king intended to confront and break Bianchi with four legions, sixteen thousand."

citations.quote: la prima legione tratteneva Neipperg; altre quattro erano a Macerata; aveva Ancona pochi presidii; tutta l’oste era forte di ventiquattromila soldati.

claims.rationale: Local command acts rather than generic army-wide credit. Author blame of subordinates and counterfactual victory claims not adopted. English rendering (ours): "Bianchi called battalions from his right; the king sent an order to Lecchi at Macerata."

claims.rationale: Attributed intention in an opponent’s retrospective; not an authenticated Austrian order. English rendering (ours): "The enemy planned to change front, throw us into the Potenza valleys, seize the main road and cut us off from Macerata, Ancona and the Abruzzi."
